canonical_title: Anthropic Claude Science in-house drug development plan
aliases: Anthropic wants to develop its own drugs
treatment: Follow-up confirmed a Bay Area wet lab and physical biology work. Do not repeat unless Anthropic gives target diseases, experimental results, lab-automation milestones, partners, clinical path, manufacturing, or material safety/research-governance changes.
known_facts: Claude Science was already known as a scientific research workbench.
The Verge reported in July that Anthropic wanted to develop its own drugs, with an initial focus on neglected diseases.

On September 18 Reuters reported, and Anthropic life sciences head Eric Kauderer-Abrams confirmed, that Anthropic has established a Bay Area wet lab and is already doing physical biology work in-house and with external partners.
Anthropic is exploring Claude-directed robotic lab execution with limited human intervention while stating that human oversight remains essential.
Anthropic says it is not running clinical trials for now and is focusing on needs that pharma and biotech companies would not otherwise address.
A spokesperson clarified that the wet lab itself is not specifically a drug-discovery lab.
reinclude_only_if: Anthropic publishes specific target diseases or experimental results.
Claude-directed robotic lab automation reaches a concrete production or autonomy milestone.
Anthropic discloses a clinical, manufacturing, or major external-partner strategy change.
A credible source reports a material safety, governance, or competitive-boundary change in the life-sciences program.
Claude Science product availability, pricing, admin enablement, or scientific workflow capability changes materially.
notes: Recovered after a scheduled LLM Night Lite run reported LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED because the old protocol tried to rewrite the full monolithic JSONL. September 18 follow-up adds confirmed wet-lab operation and physical lab automation work.
